subject.title: Telegram agent: chatbot follow-up loop + exec tool aborts on pkill against earlier-spawned process

question: Should this mixed report be split into the canonical future-follow-up policy tracker plus a separate process-control hardening item, or should maintainers define one combined invariant here?
rationale: Current source shows partial mitigations and an existing canonical follow-up-policy issue, but deciding whether raw shell `pkill` should be hardened versus steering agents to the managed `process kill` tool is product and process-control policy.

options.title: Split And Scope
options.body: Keep this issue open as the mixed field report, link the broad follow-up half to the canonical follow-up-policy tracker, and define a narrow process-control follow-up for raw kill/self-match behavior.

options.title: Use This As Canonical
options.body: Make this issue the owner for both Telegram action-only reply policy and process-control hardening, accepting a broader multi-surface fix plan.

options.title: Treat Managed Process Tool As Enough
options.body: Close only the process half as covered by `process kill` guidance and keep the reply-policy remainder tracked elsewhere, but that would leave the raw `pkill` expectation unresolved.

recommendation.title: Split And Scope
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the mixed field report, link the broad follow-up half to the canonical follow-up-policy tracker, and define a narrow process-control follow-up for raw kill/self-match behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Vignesh owns the closest current follow-up-policy mechanisms, while process-control implementation should also involve Vincent once the split is chosen.
